idioms.phraseAr: متأخر خير من ألا يأتي أبداً
idioms.meaning: It's better to do something late than not do it at all.
idioms.meaningAr: من الأفضل أن تفعل الشيء متأخراً من ألا تفعله أبداً.
idioms.example: I finished my homework at bedtime — better late than never!
idioms.exampleAr: أنهيت واجبي وقت النوم — متأخر خير من ألا يأتي أبداً!

idioms.meaning: The person we just talked about appears.
idioms.example: Speak of the devil — here he is!

idioms.meaning: Being too curious can get you into trouble.
idioms.meaningAr: الفضول الزائد قد يوقعك في المشاكل.
idioms.example: Don't open that box — curiosity killed the cat!
idioms.exampleAr: لا تفتح ذلك الصندوق — الفضول قد يوقعك في المشاكل!

idioms.meaning: To ignore someone on purpose.
idioms.example: She gave me the cold shoulder.

idioms.meaning: To study hard.
idioms.example: Exams are near — time to hit the books.

idioms.meaning: The more you practice something, the better you become at it.
idioms.meaningAr: كلما تدربت أكثر على شيء، أصبحت أفضل فيه.
idioms.example: Keep practicing your spelling — practice makes perfect!
idioms.exampleAr: استمر في التدرب على الإملاء — التمرين يقود إلى الإتقان!

idioms.meaning: To joke with someone.
idioms.example: Relax, I'm just pulling your leg!

idioms.meaning: A good thing that seemed bad at first.
idioms.meaningAr: أمر جيد بدا سيئاً في البداية.
idioms.example: Missing the bus was a blessing in disguise.

idioms.meaning: Both people are responsible for something that happens between them.
idioms.meaningAr: كلا الشخصين مسؤولان عمّا يحدث بينهما.
idioms.example: They both made the mistake — it takes two to tango.

idioms.meaning: Extremely happy.
idioms.example: She was on cloud nine after winning.
idioms.exampleAr: كانت في قمة السعادة بعد الفوز.

idioms.phrase: Bite off more than you can chew
idioms.meaning: To take on too much.
idioms.example: I bit off more than I could chew with three clubs.
idioms.exampleAr: حمّلت نفسي فوق طاقتي بثلاثة أنشطة.

idioms.meaning: A share of something.
idioms.example: Everyone wants a piece of the pie.

idioms.phrase: The apple doesn't fall far from the tree
idioms.meaning: Children are often similar to their parents.
idioms.example: She loves painting just like her mom — the apple doesn't fall far from the tree.
idioms.exampleAr: هي تحب الرسم مثل والدتها تماماً — الشبه بين الأبناء والآباء.

idioms.meaning: A very rare chance.
idioms.example: This trip is a once-in-a-lifetime chance.

idioms.meaning: Stay positive in hard times.
idioms.example: Keep your chin up — you'll pass next time.

idioms.meaning: What you do matters more than what you say.
idioms.example: He helps quietly — actions speak louder than words.
idioms.exampleAr: يساعد بهدوء — الأفعال أبلغ من الأقوال.

idioms.meaning: The final problem that ends patience.
idioms.example: That rude reply was the last straw.
idioms.exampleAr: ذلك الرد الوقح كان القشة الأخيرة.

idioms.meaning: To be undecided.
idioms.example: Don't sit on the fence — choose one.

idioms.meaning: To become uncontrollable.
idioms.example: The game got out of hand.

idioms.meaning: An event that makes you change.
idioms.example: The low grade was a wake-up call.
